details:
What It Does & How It Works

StarWay Vision Smart Systems is a 2D physics-based aerospace engineering simulation designed to model and validate Martian Entry, Descent, and Landing (EDL) impact dynamics alongside rover surface mobility. Conventional planetary landers rely on heavy, mechanically complex suspension systems that reduce scientific payload capacity. To solve this, our system models a hybrid damping architecture combining a Non-Newtonian Shear Thickening Fluid (STF) core with a reinforced titanium lattice structure.

In the simulation, the STF remains flexible during low-velocity maneuvers to absorb minor vibrations, but undergoes an instantaneous viscosity spike upon high-velocity impact—transitioning into a rigid, energy-dissipating barrier based on the power-law shear model. The surrounding titanium lattice provides structural integrity and prevents permanent deformation under multi-axis stress. Users can interactively test drop scenarios and traverse jagged Martian terrain while monitoring real-time telemetry, G-force spikes, and energy absorption rates via an integrated engineering HUD.

Benefits & Intended Impact

- Mass Optimization: Replaces bulky hydraulic shock absorbers with a lightweight, passive smart-material damping system, freeing up critical mass for scientific instruments; while the fluid core introduces a minor propellant mass penalty, it is heavily outweighed by eliminating complex mechanical assemblies and preventing catastrophic landing damage.

- Zero-Maintenance Reliability: Eliminates moving mechanical joints prone to seizing in abrasive Martian regolith and extreme cold.

- Rapid Prototyping: Provides mission planners and aerospace students with an accessible, real-time sandbox to test structural survival thresholds before costly physical fabrication.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software

- Game & Physics Engine: Godot Engine 4 (2D RigidBody and custom physics processing)

- Programming Language: GDScript (custom real-time non-Newtonian viscosity equations, telemetry logging, and HUD rendering)

- Data & Reference Sources: NASA Planetary Data System (PDS) and NASA Mars Fact Sheet

- Version Control & Distribution: GitHub (source code repository and compiled Windows executable release)

Creativity & Engineering Considerations

Our primary innovation lies in pairing a passive non-Newtonian fluid with an additively manufactured titanium lattice tailored specifically for extraterrestrial terramechanics. Throughout development, we accounted for critical Martian environmental constraints:

- Dynamic Threshold Optimization: Integrated an adaptive shear-activation threshold to prevent premature STF hardening during minor, non-critical terrain vibrations, ensuring vehicle momentum and control stability are preserved until true high-impact events occur.

- Low Gravity: Calibrated all kinematic and impact velocity equations to Martian surface gravity (-3.72 m/s²).

- Cryogenic Temperatures: Modeled silicone-oil-based carrier fluid properties capable of resisting freezing and maintaining predictable shear-thickening behavior down to -100°C.

- Surface Hazards: Designed variable terrain profiles featuring sharp basaltic rocks, craters, and uneven slopes to test both vertical drop shocks and lateral rover traversal.
